description: Write the incoming 2D geometry to an AutoCAD DXF (R12) and download it — the drawing counterpart of Export 3D. Wire a 2D Render node in and each of its rows becomes a layer.
instructions:
A SINK: wire any 2D geometry into its input and press Download .dxf. Nothing is drawn on canvas and nothing is committed — the node is invisible to the flow apart from the file it writes.

WIRE A 2D RENDER NODE IN and the export is fully described by the render rows: every row's outlines go out as closed POLYLINEs on a layer named after that row's Layer field, in the nearest AutoCAD pen colour to the row's colour, and a CIRCLE row can go out as true CIRCLE entities instead of a 64-sided polygon. Any other 2D node (Polygon, Mitered Join, Boolean 2D, BSP …) exports too — it simply has one layer instead of several.

COORDINATES are measured from the flow anchor, not from wherever the canvas happens to sit, so the drawing opens around the origin. Plan Y points DOWN; "Y up (CAD)" flips it so the DXF reads the right way up in AutoCAD / LibreCAD / QCAD, which is what you almost always want.

UNITS scale the metre coordinates on the way out — the file itself carries no unit, so pick what the receiving drawing expects (millimetres for most production CAD).
